scenes.say: Tiny specks floating in your sight? Here's when it's harmless, and when it's urgent.

scenes.en: A clear gel fills your eye. With age it shrinks, and tiny clumps cast shadows on the retina.
scenes.ta: கண்ணின் உள்ளே உள்ள ஜெல் வயதுடன் சுருங்கும்
scenes.say: Your eye is filled with a clear gel. With age, this gel slowly shrinks, and tiny clumps in it cast shadows on the retina. You see those shadows as floating specks.

scenes.en: Floaters are more common after 50 and in short-sighted people. Many fade over time.
scenes.say: Did you know? These floating specks are more common after fifty, and in people who are short-sighted. Many become less noticeable over time.

scenes.en: That can be the gel tugging on the retina.
scenes.say: Seeing flashes of light, like lightning at the edge of your vision? That can be the gel tugging on the retina.

scenes.en: A sudden shower of floaters, flashes, or a curtain-like shadow
scenes.ta: திடீர் புள்ளிகள், மின்னல், திரை போல் நிழல்: உடனே கண் மருத்துவரிடம்!
scenes.say: See an eye specialist the same day if you suddenly get a shower of new specks, flashes of light, or a dark shadow like a curtain over your vision. These can be signs of a retinal tear.

scenes.en: Check each eye alone. Note anything new. Get a dilated eye exam.
scenes.say: Check each eye separately, notice anything new, and get a dilated eye exam, so the retina can be checked properly.
